messages.subject: Computations on big shared-memory machine
parts:
I am planning to request access to a large shared-memory machine (e.g. SGI with 256 processors). 
Is there anyone with positive or negative experience about gains in computing time with INLA, in particular with the SPDE model? 

For example, how should I expect the computing time to scale with the number of cores? 

I guess this is very model- and data-dependent but any clue would be much appreciated.

Gilles

> I am planning to request access to a large shared-memory machine (e.g.

> number of cores?
>

> I guess this is very model- and data-dependent but any clue would be

the code parallize on a high level, so that operations like chol(Q) and
solve(Q,b) are not parallized, but many of those operations run at the
same time are parallized.
with this strategy I think there is a limite of how many cores the code
can really take advantage of, but also this depends on which stage in
the algorithm we talk about. to optimize theta, is usually costly, and
there it less potential of high number of cpus, whereas the integration
over many theta_j's and computing all the marginals for the latent
field, should take advantage of many cpus.

I have never ran the code on so many cpus, but I guess some tweaks are
possible to do to improve the perforance, which until now is more
optimized for 2, 4 and 8 cpus, really.
